title: A market after sunset
bodyMd:
A fictional coastal town moved its weekly market from the afternoon to the evening during summer. Stallholders welcomed the cooler temperatures, and visitor numbers rose. Yet total sales increased only slightly. Interviews suggested that many new visitors came to meet friends and listen to music rather than to buy goods. Some stallholders called the change disappointing, while nearby cafés reported busier evenings.

The town council proposed a second trial without live music to identify how much of the crowd the performances attracted. A traders’ representative objected that removing music would test a different kind of event, not merely reveal a hidden feature of the original one. The council accepted this limitation but still considered the comparison informative. It wanted to distinguish the market’s value to stallholders from its broader value as a public gathering place, rather than assume that a larger crowd necessarily benefited everyone equally.
